item.title: Women's Brick Initiative: Please provide your perspective on diversity in the LEGO hobby
item.author: MeganL
item.description:
The Women's Brick Initiative (WBI) is a Recognized Fan Community that is dedicated to empowering more women and girls in the LEGO hobby while also advocating for diversity, equity and inclusion. WBI runs an intern programme each year in partnership with Smith College. Every summer, these interns dive deep into data behind LEGO around issues on equity and inclusion.

This year's interns would like your input on two surveys!

The first survey asks how LEGO can be more inclusive. Recently we have asked WBI members what ideas they had about ways to make LEGO a more inclusive space. Combining those ideas and conversations from our team, we have devised a list of actions LEGO can take to make the community more equal and inclusive to all nationalities, races, and genders. We would like your help in ranking them. That survey can be found here.

The second survey focusses on the brick-built sculptures that are found at many retail establishments that sell LEGO. These sculptures are often some of the most memorable parts of visiting a LEGO retail space. They can celebrate local culture, bring familiar characters to life, and make each store feel different from simply shopping online. We are inviting LEGO fans and store visitors around the world to help us build a global collection of LEGO retail sculptures. The second survey can be found here.

We're asking for all responses to be submitted by September 18, 2026. Preliminary results of the first survey will be presented by one of the interns at Skaerbaek Fan Weekend.

Thank you for your help! Any questions, please contact me directly.

item.title: Review: 11386 SpongeBob SquarePants: Bikini Bottom
item.author: TheBrickPal
item.description:
Are ya ready, kids?

Since 1999, Nickelodeon's SpongeBob SquarePants has delighted kids and kids-at-heart with its absurd humor, fun storylines, and lovable characters. In 2006, LEGO gave us a theme based on the show, consisting of just fourteen sets. The line unceremoniously ended in 2012, with lots of untapped potential.

Fourteen years later, LEGO SpongeBob is back, with 11386 SpongeBob SquarePants: Bikini Bottom! There's a lot riding on this return, with so much nostalgia for both the show and original sets, and many developments in building techniques, not to mention an expanded color palette. Did they pull off the Conch Street set of our dreams? There's only one way to find out: by diving in! So come on, let's have the best day ever...

item.title: Decorating your LEGO space
item.author: Yellowcastle
item.description:
There is no one right way to enjoy LEGO. I suspect this is why our beloved hobby has found such widespread popularity these days. We buy and build, and play and display. We collect and store, and part and sort. We MOC and show, and invest and sell. We go to Brickset and read and write, and laud and gripe.

For many, our relationship with LEGO evolves over time and is often dictated by the constraints of our everyday lives. Many of us start out building, playing, tearing down, reimagining, and then building again. As we get older, we have less and less time to build, let alone design or play.

As Father Time ticks, ticks away, I find it more and more difficult to keep LEGO a part of my daily life... that is, until I found my newest passion: decorating my LEGO space.

item.title: Review: 75455 Boba Fett
item.author: CapnRex101
item.description:
There have been a substantial number of large-scale characters produced this year, sometimes to the point of them becoming rather repetitive. 75455 Boba Fett definitely stands out from this crowded field though, potentially looking more authentic than any other LEGO statue!

The vibrant colours of Boba Fett's armour work brilliantly for a model of this scale and I like the pose too, which looks fairly realistic. We have seen droids represented accurately by this kind of statue, although I doubted whether a human character, even an armoured one, could ever look as impressive as Boba Fett does.
